explanation: Green peppercorns are picked unripe and kept green, black ones are unripe berries dried until dark, and white ones are ripe seeds with the skin removed. Pink peppercorns come from a different plant.

claims.text: Black, white and green peppercorns are all fruits of the same plant, the vine Piper nigrum.
Green peppercorns are unripe fruits preserved so they stay green.
Black peppercorns are unripe fruits dried until their skins turn dark.
White peppercorns are ripe fruits with the outer skin removed.
Pink peppercorns are the fruits of a different plant, the Peruvian or Brazilian pepper tree (Schinus).

evidence.restatement: Green peppercorns are unripe fruits kept green by brining, freeze-drying or dehydrating.
Black peppercorns are unripe fruits dried until the skin turns dark and wrinkled.
White peppercorns are ripe fruits soaked and stripped of their outer skin, leaving the seed.
Pink peppercorns come from Schinus, the Peruvian or Brazilian pepper tree.
Black, green and white peppercorns are all fruits of Piper nigrum, differing only in ripeness and processing.

claimResults.note: Pink peppercorns come from a different plant but are not in the statement. High-risk claim: my knowledge check counts only together with external evidence in the other check (section 9.5.3).

evidence.restatement: Green peppercorns are picked unripe and preserved, for example by brining or freeze-drying, so they stay green.
Black peppercorns are picked just before ripeness, blanched and dried until the skins darken.
White peppercorns are ripe fruits with the outer skin removed, often by soaking.
Pink peppercorns are usually the fruit of Schinus trees, the Peruvian or Brazilian pepper tree.

claimResults.note: Ripe red Piper nigrum berries are also sold as red peppercorns; 'pink peppercorns' in the usual sense are Schinus.
